title: Under the Haswell dependent-latency profile, byte reversal has minimum cost 4
statement: With costs vpshufb=1, vpermd=3, vpermq=3, vpalignr=1, vperm2i128=3 (Intel documented register-form latencies, a serial dependency-chain proxy), no sequence in the unary five-family language reverses 32 tags at total cost <= 3, and vpermd; vpshufb does it at cost 4. The cost bound is composed as a checked weighted-at-most CNF over the same formula.

formal.statement: encode_weighted_unary_avx2_sequence(target=reversed, bound=3, profile=intel-haswell-dependent-latency-cycles) is UNSAT; bound=4 is SAT.

scope: Same language as M.avx2.reverse.len2.unary5; profile intel-haswell-dependent-latency-cycles; NOT throughput, port pressure, or whole-machine cost.

evidence.note: 6,024 vars / 235,303 clauses; CaDiCaL 3.0.1 UNSAT in 1.35 s; 12,554,825-byte DRAT accepted by axeyum backward checker; a 2-byte and a 64-byte truncation are both REJECTED (verified here). The formula is NOT UP-refutable, so this proof is load-bearing.

provenance.by: isa-calculus bootstrap (Claude Code session with axeyum)
